sb_prompt: COMPARE YOUR OPINIONS AND THOSE OF THE OTHER CALLER ON CAPITAL PUNISHMENT.  DO EITHER OF YOU THINK IT SHOULD BE RESTRICTED TO CERTAIN CRIMES OR CIRCUMSTANCES?  HOW DO THE POLICIES AND PRACTICES OF YOUR STATE FIT WITH YOUR OPINIONS?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hey there.
ParticipantA: You got my number from somewhere? I'm the carpenter, if you're wondering.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I got it from the list. I'm a real estate agent.
ParticipantA: Right. Okay. So the prompt was about capital punishment?
ParticipantB: Yeah. That's the heavy stuff, isn't it?
ParticipantA: It is. I've got mixed feelings on it, honestly. Parts of it sit fine with me, parts don't.
ParticipantB: I know that feeling. I have mixed feelings too, but I made up my mind years ago.
ParticipantA: Made up your mind? You didn't change your view?
ParticipantB: No, not really. It just seemed like the right path to me back then. I can't really say why now, though.
ParticipantA: That's weird. I actually know someone close to me who went through it.
ParticipantB: Oh man, really? Someone you know well?
ParticipantA: Yeah, his dad. He was on death row for a long time. It messed with my head a lot.
ParticipantB: That's heavy. Did you go visit him?
ParticipantA: A few times. Just to see him, not really to talk about the death part.
ParticipantB: I can imagine that. When you saw him, did it make you want to stop it all?
ParticipantA: Sometimes. But other times, I thought if we don't do it, the victims' families don't get justice.
ParticipantB: That's the tricky part, isn't it? Justice versus just ending a life.
ParticipantA: Exactly. I don't think it should be used for every crime, though.
ParticipantB: Agreed. I think it should be restricted to murder, maybe? Not for drugs or theft.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I think we should only do it for intentional murder where there was no doubt.
ParticipantB: That sounds fair. My state is all over the place though. They do it for some things, but the jury can't agree on much.
ParticipantA: What's your state like?
ParticipantB: It's pretty strict here. We have a lot of executions, but lately it's been stuck on death row people for a long time.
ParticipantA: That doesn't sit well with me. If they wait ten years, what's the point?
ParticipantB: Yeah, that's the thing. If they're innocent, it's too late. I don't want that on my conscience.
ParticipantA: That makes sense. I'd prefer to stick to the life sentence for those cases.
ParticipantB: Me too. Honestly, I think keeping them alive is better than risking a mistake.
ParticipantA: I guess I can see that now. My guy's dad got out eventually, so that helped.
ParticipantB: Oh, really? You're lucky he didn't stay.
ParticipantA: Yeah, that was the only part that made me feel okay about the system, in a way.
ParticipantB: Good. Maybe that's enough for both of us.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I think so. Thanks for talking it over.
ParticipantB: No problem. You too.
